purpose: Check the source-level fish-name forms from the 2020 and 2021 Sawaga papers against selected Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes records and a peer-reviewed Philippine fish checklist, while preserving study-specific spellings, color forms and conflicting IDs.

studySources.sourceContext: Results prose from the 2018-2019 survey; its extracted Table 1 cells were unavailable. Amatitlania nigrofasciata appears as two color-form count categories, and Xiphophorous hellerii is a source spelling.
Separate preliminary report of 2020-2021 observations and source labels. It is not used to correct or add counts to the earlier survey.

authorities.name: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes
authorities.institution: California Academy of Sciences, Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability
authorities.accessMethod: Selected official Catalog name records were reviewed through indexed excerpts. One historical combination, Nomorhamphus pectoralis, was also checked in a 2025 peer-reviewed Philippine fish checklist. This is a nomenclatural screen only; no specimens, images, tissues or museum vouchers were accessed.
authorities.reuse: No item-specific permission to republish Catalog text or the checklist was verified. Only brief attributed nomenclatural outcomes and links are recorded.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Amatitlania nigrofasciata (2020: black-striped and yellowish color-form categories; 2021: two reported specimens)
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: One accepted taxon name; the two color-form count categories in the 2020 prose are not separate species. This nomenclature does not establish that the 2018-2019 samples were identified correctly.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The 2025 peer-reviewed annotated checklist crosswalks the original combination Dermogenys pectoralis to Nomorhamphus pectoralis.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: This supports the name combination only; it does not establish identity of the Sawaga fish.

nameCrosswalk.sourceLabel: Xiphophorous hellerii (2020 Results spelling); Xiphophorus hellerii (2021)
nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog accepts Xiphophorus hellerii. The 2020 Results spelling Xiphophorous is a source typo candidate; preserve it in provenance.
Valid as printed at species level.
Valid as printed in the selected Catalog record.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: The 2021 report instead labels a separate Sawaga fish P. disjunctivus. Both are accepted species names; no voucher crosswalk establishes whether the 2020 fish was misidentified.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: Valid as printed and distinct from P. pardalis.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: The name cross-check cannot determine which species was present in the 2018-2019 sample.

nameCrosswalk.catalogOutcome: The Catalog treats the source spelling bengalensis as a spelling variant and lists Ophisternon bengalense as valid.
nameCrosswalk.interpretation: Candidate nomenclatural normalization only; no Sawaga specimen was reidentified.

interpretation.taxonomy: The checked source name-forms map to ten current taxonomic candidates across the two reports, after counting the 2020 Amatitlania color-form categories as one taxon name. This does not resolve the 2020 paper's 8-versus-7-name discrepancy.
interpretation.crossStudyConflicts: The papers use N. pectoralis versus N. philippinus and P. pardalis versus P. disjunctivus. The authority confirms that these are separate names/taxa, but only vouchers, diagnostic images or author field records could resolve the source identifications.
interpretation.specimenIdentity: No source label was changed in place, and no specimen, image or voucher was reidentified.
interpretation.localPresence: A catalog name, reported distribution or source paper does not establish current Sawaga River presence or distribution along the whole river.
interpretation.publication: Name status does not approve reuse of study tables, photographs, occurrence claims or derived app content.

limitations: The 2020 publisher PDF download was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge; the author-uploaded text omits Table 1 cells and is marked as potentially copyrighted.
Nomenclature cannot resolve the 2020 paper's eight-species claim versus the seven unique binomials visible in its Results prose.
The Catalog cross-check cannot resolve N. pectoralis versus N. philippinus or P. pardalis versus P. disjunctivus at the specimen level.
No museum accessions, diagnostic preserved specimens, or a cross-paper field-log crosswalk were verified.
No current occurrence, native/non-native status, introduction pathway, impact, diet, safety, legal or geometry claim is inferred from name authorities.

references.supports: 2020 paper metadata and abstract, including its eight-species/family/genus summary.
Accessible 2020 Results prose names, color-form categories, reported individual counts and Xiphophorous source spelling.
Separate 2021 report's Sawaga labels and the differing N. philippinus, P. disjunctivus and O. bengalensis forms.
Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes authority and name-search interface.
2025 checklist crosswalk from Dermogenys pectoralis to Nomorhamphus pectoralis.
